strengths: Introduces a novel mesh tokenization scheme based on vertex layering/sorting and compressed self-layer/between-layer adjacency matrices, encoding each vertex once and reducing redundant vertex tokens.
Achieves a compression ratio of 0.22 and provides a detailed derivation showing about 2 tokens per face, competitive with the strongest prior compression methods.
The connected-component-aware token design is a useful inductive bias, helping the model generate small but semantically important components (e.g., eyes, accessories).
The non-manifold edge processing and manifold-oriented representation are practically relevant for downstream tasks such as UV unwrapping, simulation, and 3D printing.
Quantitative results show improvements over EdgeRunner, TreeMeshGPT, and BPT on CD, HD, NC, and |NC|, with especially clear gains in normal consistency.
Qualitative comparisons demonstrate detailed, visually coherent meshes and highlight non-manifold artifacts in some local-patch baselines.
The paper is generally well written, with method details, training setup, and derivations documented in the main text and appendix.
The method has clear relevance to auto-regressive 3D mesh generation and addresses important limitations of prior tree-traversal and local-patch tokenizers.
weaknesses: The main compression claim is overstated: Table 1 lists TreeMeshGPT with the same 0.22 compression ratio as the proposed method, yet the abstract/introduction imply that existing methods always repeat vertex tokens and that the method achieves state-of-the-art compression.

The quantitative comparison is not fully apples-to-apples: only EdgeRunner is marked as faithfully trained on the same dataset, while TreeMeshGPT and BPT appear to be evaluated under different training settings, making the reported gains difficult to attribute to the tokenizer alone.

There is no ablation on the core tokenization design: no controlled study of layer ordering, self-layer vs. between-layer compression, non-manifold processing, connected-component tokens, window sizes, or vocabulary choices. Only the resampling strategy is ablated.

Topological advantages are not quantitatively evaluated: the paper claims manifold topology, watertightness support, and consistent face normals, but reports only NC/|NC| and qualitative figures. Metrics such as manifold-edge ratio, watertight ratio, flipped-triangle ratio, and connected-component accuracy are missing.

The new FR metric is not convincingly justified: a higher predicted-to-ground-truth face ratio can reflect over-generation rather than better geometric detail, and no quality-cost tradeoff is analyzed.

The evaluation is limited to point-cloud-conditioned generation on 500 gObjaverse meshes; text- and image-conditioned results are shown only qualitatively in the appendix, without quantitative comparison.
No error bars or statistical significance tests are reported for the main metrics, despite small differences between some methods (e.g., CD 0.079 vs. 0.080 over BPT).

Reproducibility is currently limited: code/checkpoints are promised but not yet released, and the model requires substantial compute (500M parameters, 16 H800 GPUs for 15 days), which may hinder verification.

The method has practical constraints that may limit generalization: vocabulary size up to 10,267, a predefined maximum vertices-per-layer m=200, and dataset filtering that excludes meshes exceeding this limit.
The paper does not discuss failure cases or robustness of the non-manifold processing and tokenization under noisy or degenerate meshes, which are common in real-world 3D datasets.

strengths: Introduces a nontrivial mesh tokenization scheme based on vertex layering, self-layer/between-layer adjacency compression, and connected-component tokens, which is a plausible direction for compact autoregressive mesh generation.

The non-manifold edge preprocessing via edge graph partitioning is carefully designed with multiple rules (max cycle/chain first, mesh connected component first, BFS processing) and addresses a real issue for manifold mesh tokenization.
Connected-component-aware generation may help preserve small but important mesh parts; the qualitative examples illustrate this intended capability.

The method supports desirable geometric properties such as consistent face orientation and potential watertight repair detection, with some illustrative examples and a plausible half-edge-based explanation.
The paper provides appendix details on compression and preprocessing, and uses standard metrics CD/HD/NC/|NC| plus a new FR metric.
Experimental results show improvements over BPT and EdgeRunner* on CD/HD/NC/|NC| and competitive qualitative results, though not decisively.
weaknesses: The central compression claim is overstated or unsupported. Table 1 reports TreeMeshGPT also achieving 0.22 compression ratio, so the claimed state-of-the-art 22% compression is not unique; the abstract's claim of reducing token sequence redundancy by 50% is inconsistent with the BPT 0.26 to 0.22 improvement (~15%).

Evaluation is insufficient for a top-tier venue: quantitative comparison is only on 500 gObjaverse meshes despite training on multiple datasets; no per-dataset or per-category results are given; baselines are not consistently retrained or ablated; DeepMesh is only qualitative.

Topological claims are not quantitatively evaluated. Manifoldness, watertightness, and normal consistency are central, but only NC/|NC| are reported; there is no manifoldness rate, non-manifold edge count, watertightness rate, or repair success rate, and watertight repair is shown only as an illustrative example.

The new FR metric is questionable as defined (predicted/GT face count, marked ↑). Higher FR can simply indicate over-tessellation or hallucinated faces rather than better geometric fidelity; no face precision/recall or validity-aware metric is provided.

The ablation study is minimal: only the resampling strategy is ablated. There is no ablation on layer ordering, self/between-layer compression window sizes, connected-component tokens, non-manifold preprocessing, or token packing, and no complexity or robustness analysis.

Reproducibility is limited: code and checkpoints are not available; training requires 16 H800 GPUs for 15 days; key implementation details for baselines and data filtering are insufficient for exact reproduction.

Technical presentation has ambiguities and inconsistencies: the token count per vertex versus the compression derivation (4 tokens per vertex vs ~2 tokens per face) is confusing, and the compression ratio derivation relies on regularity assumptions that may not hold for generated meshes.
Positioning against the closest work, TreeMeshGPT, is inadequate given the same reported compression ratio; the novelty relative to TreeMeshGPT and BPT needs clearer differentiation.

strengths: Introduces a novel layer-based mesh tokenization that encodes each vertex once, reducing redundant vertex information by about 50% and achieving a compression ratio of 0.22, which is competitive with recent methods.
The method is connected-component aware via special tokens, which helps capture small but critical mesh parts that are often missed by baselines.

Provides useful geometric properties such as manifold topology support, watertight detection/repair, and consistent face normal orientation, which are important for downstream applications like 3D printing and UV unwrapping.
Reports quantitative improvements over strong autoregressive mesh generation baselines on CD, HD, NC, and |NC|, and provides qualitative comparisons showing better detail and manifold structure.
Includes a detailed appendix, ablation on the resampling strategy, and extensive implementation details that aid understanding of the method.
weaknesses: The claimed state-of-the-art compression ratio of 0.22 ties TreeMeshGPT in Table 1, so the uniqueness of the compression contribution is overstated; the redundancy reduction relative to TreeMeshGPT is not clearly quantified.

Baseline fairness is uncertain: only EdgeRunner is marked as faithfully retrained on the same dataset, while TreeMeshGPT and BPT are not starred, and DeepMesh is compared only qualitatively. This weakens the quantitative comparison.

Quantitative evaluation is limited to 500 randomly sampled gObjaverse meshes, despite using ShapeNetV2, 3D-FUTURE, and Toys4K in training; no quantitative results are reported on these other reserved datasets.

The manifold, watertightness, and normal consistency claims are not quantitatively evaluated beyond NC/|NC|; there are no error rates for non-manifold edges, watertightness, repair success, or topology validity on generated meshes.

The face number ratio (FR) metric is questionable: FR > 1 is interpreted as better new face generation ability, but generating more faces than ground truth may simply reflect over-tessellation rather than improved geometric fidelity.
Ablation is limited to the resampling strategy; there is no ablation on core tokenization components, window sizes, connected-component tokens, or non-manifold processing.
Reproducibility is a concern: training requires 16 H800 GPUs for about 15 days, and code/checkpoints are not provided at submission time (only promised).
The method introduces a large vocabulary of up to 10,267 tokens and requires predefining a maximum number of vertices per layer, which may limit generalization and efficiency in practice.

strengths: Presents a novel mesh tokenization algorithm based on vertex layering/sorting and layer adjacency matrix compression, with a clear conceptual framing and canonical topological structure.
Achieves strong compression efficiency: 0.22 compression ratio and 26.65 bits-per-face, competitive with or better than baselines under the bits-per-face metric.

The tokenization is designed to support manifoldness, watertightness detection/repair, consistent face normals, and connected-component/part awareness, which are important downstream properties not simultaneously handled by prior tokenization methods.
Introduces practical data-processing components: online non-manifold edge processing and progressive-balanced resampling, with ablations showing improved generalization and training data scale.

Provides extensive implementation details, appendices with pseudocode, complexity analysis, ablation studies, and qualitative results across point-cloud conditioned, text-conditioned, and image-conditioned generation.
Quantitative results show slightly better CD/HD and normal consistency than strong baselines on the evaluated benchmark.
weaknesses: The central topological claims are not directly or quantitatively evaluated on generated outputs. There are no reported percentages of generated meshes that are manifold, watertight, face-normal consistent, or part-aware; Table 1 summarizes intended properties rather than empirical evidence.

The comparison protocol is not fully fair or transparent. EdgeRunner is retrained on the same dataset, but TreeMeshGPT and BPT are not retrained, and DeepMesh is omitted from quantitative comparison, weakening the quantitative conclusions.

Table 2 appears internally inconsistent: TreeMeshGPT has Bits-per-face 42.000 and token-per-face 6 under the stated formula, which would imply a compression ratio of about 0.67 if the stated definition (token length / (9 * faces)) is used, yet the table reports 0.22. This needs correction/clarification and affects the SOTA compression claim.

The 'lossless' compression claim is misleading without qualification: the method uses 7-bit quantization and is therefore lossy relative to original mesh geometry; 'lossless' likely holds only up to quantization, but this is not clearly stated.

The manuscript does not clearly explain how triangle faces are reconstructed losslessly from encoded vertex positions and edge/adjacency matrices. Since a set of vertices and edges does not generally determine a unique triangulation, the decoding/face-filling rule needs formal specification and proof.

Manifoldness, watertightness, and face-normal consistency are claimed to be guaranteed by construction, but the decoding process and any constrained decoding/repair rules are not specified with enough rigor to justify these guarantees for arbitrary predicted token sequences.

The non-manifold processing algorithm is heuristic and evaluated only via a fine-tuning ablation on a subset; there is no direct metric of surface integrity/fragmentation relative to Libigl or other processing baselines beyond qualitative examples.

The method requires a large vocabulary (10,267) and predefined maximum layer/matrix sizes (m=200), discarding meshes outside these limits; this may limit practical scalability to high-resolution or complex meshes, as acknowledged by the authors.

The resampling strategy is a straightforward application of existing long-tail sampling, and the model architecture is standard; the main novelty rests on tokenization, so the broader methodological contribution is narrower.

No code or artifact release is mentioned, and training required 16 H800 GPUs for ~15 days, which limits reproducibility and adoption. Some conditional-generation components rely on external models, which may not be reproducible.

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem: preserving application-friendly topology in autoregressive mesh generation, rather than treating meshes as unstructured triangle soups.

The proposed vertex layering and layer-adjacency matrix compression is a novel and explicit tokenization scheme, avoiding a learned VQ-VAE and achieving competitive compression efficiency in terms of bits-per-face.

The method aims to support several geometric properties simultaneously (manifoldness, watertightness, face-normal consistency, and connected-component awareness), which is a meaningful direction for practical mesh generation.

The paper includes an online non-manifold processing algorithm and a progressive resampling strategy, with some ablation evidence that scaling training data and resampling improve generation quality on complex meshes.
Qualitative results show detailed meshes and small connected components, suggesting the approach can capture some part-level structure that baselines may miss.
The appendix provides useful implementation details, complexity analysis, and pseudocode for the core tokenization algorithm.
weaknesses: The central topology-preservation claims are not quantitatively evaluated. There is no metric for manifoldness, watertightness, part awareness, or flipped-face rate on generated meshes; Table 1 is essentially a self-reported checklist, and NC/|NC| do not directly measure watertightness or valid manifold topology.

The quantitative comparison is not a fair controlled evaluation. Only EdgeRunner is retrained on the same dataset and training regime; TreeMeshGPT and BPT numbers appear to come from different settings, while DeepMesh and Nautilus are omitted. This undermines the claimed SOTA comparison.

The non-manifold processing ablation does not validate the proposed non-manifold algorithm against a baseline such as Libigl or a naive edge-splitting/merging approach. It only compares all data versus manifold-only data, so the algorithmic contribution is not isolated or supported.

The autoregressive validity of the token packing is unclear. Self-layer topology tokens may encode connections to later vertices in the same layer, yet tokens are emitted per-vertex before those future vertices are generated. The paper does not convincingly establish that decoding is causal or that future same-layer connectivity is available at prediction time.

The compression claims are oversold. The compression ratio is tied with TreeMeshGPT (0.22), and the improvement is mainly in bits-per-face, which depends on vocabulary size and comparison assumptions. The paper does not clearly demonstrate decisive superiority.

There is no downstream application evaluation despite motivating watertightness and part awareness through 3D printing, animation rigging, and robotics manipulation. The practical utility of the claimed properties remains unverified.

The paper overclaims 'lossless' compression while using 7-bit vertex quantization, and it conflates connected components with semantic part awareness. These claims require stronger definition and evidence.

Reproducibility is limited: the model is trained for 15 days on 16 H800 GPUs, no code or model release is mentioned, and critical details of baseline training and topology-repair procedures are incomplete. The writing also contains several clarity and consistency issues.

strengths: Proposes a novel mesh tokenization framework based on vertex layering/ordering and layer-adjacency matrix compression, giving a canonical topological structure for auto-regressive mesh generation.
Achieves strong compression performance (0.22 Compression Ratio and 26.65 Bits-per-face) and improves geometric metrics such as CD, HD, NC, and |NC| over several baselines.

Supports multiple desirable geometric properties simultaneously, including manifoldness, watertightness, face-normal consistency, and part awareness, which prior tokenization methods do not all provide.
Introduces an online non-manifold processing algorithm and progressive-balanced resampling strategy, with ablations showing benefits for using non-manifold data and long-tailed mesh complexity.
Provides extensive appendix material with pseudocode, complexity analysis, compression derivations, additional ablations, failure cases, and qualitative results.
Qualitative results demonstrate part-aware generation and better capture of small connected components compared with baselines such as BPT.
weaknesses: The central claim of topology preservation is not quantitatively evaluated on generated meshes: there are no measurements of manifoldness rate, watertightness rate, non-manifold edge/vertex counts, orientation consistency, or part-awareness accuracy. Table 1 is an assertion rather than an empirical measurement.

The manifold and watertight guarantees are asserted but not formally proved; the decoding process can in principle predict inconsistent adjacency matrices, and the watertight repair procedure is not fully specified or validated.

Baseline comparisons are only partially fair: only EdgeRunner is retrained on the same dataset, while TreeMeshGPT and BPT are not retrained under identical settings. Important recent baselines such as MeshAnything v2 and Nautilus are not quantitatively compared.

The compression claim is weakened by the fact that the Compression Ratio merely ties TreeMeshGPT at 0.22, and the Bits-per-face improvement over BPT is modest; the method also requires a very large vocabulary of 10,267 tokens.
Evaluation is limited to 500 meshes from gObjaverse, with no cross-dataset generalization test, no user study, no inference-speed analysis, and no direct topological evaluation.

Novelty is moderate: the core building blocks (BFS layering, binary window compression, RLE/stars-and-bars, non-manifold repair) are largely engineering adaptations and refinements of existing tokenization and geometry-processing ideas.

The claims of part awareness and online non-manifold processing are not directly measured; connected components may not correspond to semantic parts, and the non-manifold algorithm is compared mainly against Libigl rather than broader robust repair methods.
Reproducibility is limited by the extensive compute requirement (16×H800 for about 15 days), no released code/weights, and a complex multi-dataset pipeline.
The presentation is dense, and critical details about triangle decoding, face inference, and topology-preservation mechanisms are relegated to the appendix or left unclear in the main text.
